A module is simply a directory containing the files Lunar needs to build a software package, and optionally patches and configuration files.

Only DETAILS is required. For everything else Lunar has a default, so a module needs a file only where the default doesn't fit. Many modules have just DETAILS and DEPENDS, plus a short BUILD that adds a few options.
- Sets version, source URL(s) and other critical data
- Specifies modules which must (will) be removed by module
- Reacts when other modules are installed or removed (rebuild, remove, toggle an optional dependency, run a script)
- Asks the user questions that set build options
- Prepares the source: unpacking, extra sources, edits
- Runs necessary variations on: configure; make; make install
- Rarely needed; runs after BUILD while files are still tracked
- Messages, notes, more cleanups, configuration fixes

The DEPENDS file is essential to configuration management and is the key to the overall operation of Lunar. Dependencies should be exactly specified, preferably not assuming the presence of any other modules, while knowing the sub-dependencies of the modules which are added and not adding those explicitly where not needed.
Getting this right is difficult. Because the state of installed packages may vary widely, it's important to have a good understanding of what might or might not be installed on a target system.

POST_BUILD runs after BUILD, while Lunar is still recording installed files. After it, Lunar runs its own post-build steps: it installs the files from the module's directories (

POST_BUILD is rarely needed, and only a handful of modules have one. Install files in BUILD instead (remember not to overwrite existing configuration files), or install defaults from POST_INSTALL (again, not overwriting files that are already there).
POST_INSTALL runs after the module is installed, to finish setting it up. Its changes aren't recorded as part of the module, so
won't undo them; this makes it the place for things that should survive a removal or that depend on the machine.

# /var/lib/lunar/moonbase/doc-tools/man/POST_INSTALL
if module_installed xserver; then
  if [ ! -e "/etc/man.conf" ] ; then
    cd /etc &&
    ln -sf /usr/share/misc/man.conf man.conf
  fi
fi

Keep module directories small: every moonbase update downloads them. A large patch or extra file belongs on a server, as an extra source (
. Because Lunar recorded every file the module installed, most of the removal is automatic. PRE_REMOVE and POST_REMOVE handle anything else.
PRE_REMOVE runs before the module's files are removed. Use it to stop or undo things that need the module's files to still be there.

# /var/lib/lunar/moonbase/net/resolvconf/PRE_REMOVE
resolvconf --wipe-runtime-directories &&
rmdir "`readlink /etc/resolvconf/run`" &&

if [ -L /etc/resolv.conf ] && [ "`readlink /etc/resolv.conf`" = "/etc/resolvconf/run/resolv.conf" ]; then
  rm /etc/resolv.conf
fi &&

if [ -e /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/original ]; then
  cp /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/original /etc/resolv.conf
fi
POST_REMOVE runs after the files are removed. Use it to remove data that wasn't recorded and to adjust remaining configuration files and data.
PRE_REMOVE and POST_REMOVE don't run when
